editorial:
You follow two friends, Tara and Dawn, as they cross paths with Art the Clown on Halloween night. The movie wastes no time and throws you into a dark, bloody chase through empty streets and old buildings. Art never speaks, but his creepy smile and wild actions make every scene feel tense. The story is simple, so you can focus on the scares and the survival fight. It feels like a throwback slasher with a mean streak.

The acting is rough in spots, but David Howard Thornton makes Art unforgettable. The pacing stays fast, with long, brutal set pieces that push your limits. The gore is heavy, so sensitive viewers should skip it. If you love old-school slashers and want a wild night, this is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Art the Clown kills Tara and Dawn after a long chase, then faces the police. He is shot and taken to the morgue, but he is not dead. He sits up, kills the coroner, and walks away into the night. The twist is that Art cannot be stopped by normal means, so the terror is far from over for everyone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves extreme slasher horror.
